Situation1: A family member has a significant event they want to share with everyone.
Expectation2: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation2: The mandatory daily pre-work safety briefing is starting in two minutes.
Story: I stood at the edge of the construction site, the morning air thick with the smell of concrete and dust. My phone buzzed in my pocket—my daughter’s name flashed on the screen. I answered, and her voice trembled with excitement. “Dad, can you put me on speaker? We want to tell everyone together—Maya got into college!” I could hear my granddaughter giggling in the background, waiting for my reaction. My heart swelled with pride, but I glanced at the foreman waving us over. The safety briefing was about to start, and missing it meant risking a write-up or worse. My crew counted on me to be there, to set an example. But my family expected me to be present, to share in this milestone. I felt torn, the weight of my hard hat pressing down as much as the expectations from both sides. My thumb hovered over the phone, caught between the joy of my family and the responsibility of my team, unsure which world I belonged to in that moment.
